clue.text: Answer from helpline base usual taped reply horror: so a '''ello?'" wasted

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined and broken up, so the long run of fodder words is smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the policeman's ''ello', taken as written with its dropped H

explanation.surface: A caller's frustration at hearing the usual taped reply on a helpline, with a comic copper's ''ello?' thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirty-two letters of BASE USUAL TAPED REPLY HORROR SO A ELLO, shuffled by 'wasted', spell out the whole recorded message across five linked lights.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the familiar recorded message a caller hears while queueing on a telephone support line.

clue.text: See 1 across
I draw the line out East over penny dreadful

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' sends the preceding letters upwards, so they are read backwards
the East letter is put out of the word that means draw the line

parts.note: to rule is to draw a straight line
E is the compass abbreviation for East
D is the abbreviation for an old penny (Latin denarius)

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to cheapen themselves with a penny dreadful, the lurid Victorian pulp novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from RULE leaving RUL; I + RUL turned upwards by 'over' gives LURI. 'Penny dreadful' looks like one phrase but splits into D and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shockingly sensational, which is what dreadful pulp fiction was meant to be.

clue.text: A quiet guest reappearing to steal the show

indicators.note: the letters reappear in a new order, signalling an anagram

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A guest who had slipped away comes back quietly and becomes the centre of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to draw attention away from them, stealing the show.

clue.text: See 1 across
He discovered chloroform lake: that's great!

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
i.e. (id est) means 'that is'
big means great in size

explanation.surface: An excited exclamation about a chemist's discovery of chloroform beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Justus von Liebig, the German chemist, prepared chloroform in 1831, independently of others.
explanation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig is one of the chemists credited with first making chloroform, a factual description of a person.

clue.text: Top Iranian child minder accommodating a Scot!

indicators.note: the nanny word accommodates, holding the other letters inside it

parts.note: an ayah is a nanny or nursemaid in India
a scot is an old word for a tax or levy, the same as a toll (as in 'scot-free')

explanation.surface: A senior Iranian cleric's nanny has a Scotsman lodging with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot' is not a Scotsman but the old word for a tax, as in 'scot-free'. An ayah was a nanny employed by families in colonial India.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a high-ranking Shia cleric in Iran, a top religious authority there.

clue.text: Like those effete Romantiques on pot, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be spoken and heard rather than read

parts.note: being on pot means being on weed, cannabis

explanation.surface: A jibe that languid French Romantic types were simply stoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a French accent, 'on weed' sounds like ENNUIED, a jokey adjective from ennui: bored and world-weary.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete Romantics affected weary boredom, so they were full of ennui, a fanciful participle-adjective.

clue.text: Today's leading man? Ah! Just imagine! 'e could be, if the other one left

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else, so this signals an anagram

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a cocky chap might be the star of the day, if only his rival stepped aside.
explanation.walkthrough: AH JUST IMAGINE E, shuffled by 'could be', holds the answer plus one I: 'if the other one left' takes out the spare I. James Naughtie presented BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
explanation.definitionFit: James Naughtie was a lead presenter of BBC Radio 4's morning news show Today, so he was its leading man.

clue.text: King appearing from the wings of a jet

definitions.meaning: the tragic Shakespearean monarch with three daughters

definitions.text: appearing from the wings of a jet
definitions.meaning: the name painted on the private Learjet

explanation.surface: A stage king makes his entrance from the wings, with an aircraft in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings' suggests a theatre's side stage where a king actor appears; the second sense is the maker's name on a Learjet.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is the title monarch of Shakespeare's tragedy, a royal personage.

clue.text: Ashes near win is lacking destructive bowler

indicators.note: destructive suggests the words are broken up, signalling an anagram

parts.note: taken as written; 'lacking' says these letters are absent from the result

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: the Ashes are nearly won, but a destructive bowler is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: ASHES NEAR WIN less I and S ('lacking is') rearranges to the answer. The Ashes is the England-Australia Test cricket series; Shane Warne was Australia's great leg-spin bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Shane Warne was a famous Australian leg-spinner, one of cricket's greatest bowlers.

clue.text: The one enlightened theologian consumed by a radiant reversal

indicators.note: the theologian letters are swallowed up inside the other piece
reversal tells you to read the preceding letters backwards

parts.note: a hub is the centre from which spokes radiate
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A theologian is overwhelmed by a dazzling change of heart and feels enlightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radiant' looks like an adjective for the reversal, but stands for the centre of a wheel, from which spokes radiate.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddha means 'the awakened one', the title of Siddhartha Gautama who attained enlightenment.

clue.text: Is copied out in parts

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A document has been transcribed piecemeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic describes something told in separate episodes, that is in parts.

clue.text: How to enter Queer Street? Certainly not!

definitions.meaning: Queer Street is old British slang for debt and hard times, entered by having no money

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to fall into poverty and is firmly rebuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a pun: you get to Queer Street, British slang for financial trouble, with no means.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic negative, and literally describes having no means or money.

clue.text: See 1 across
The force of Enid Blyton?

parts.note: British slang for the police, from the policeman Mr ___ in Enid Blyton's Noddy books

explanation.surface: A question about the police force in a children's author's books.
explanation.walkthrough: Enid Blyton was an English children's author; her Noddy stories feature a slow-witted village policeman whose name became slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Plod is British slang for the police, from the Noddy books' constable.

clue.text: He scored with workers' 'ousing

indicators.note: housing with its H dropped tells you to drop the H from the word for workers' housing too

parts.note: worker bees are housed in hives

explanation.surface: A composer who wrote music about workers' housing, said in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Workers are worker bees, whose housing is HIVES; the dropped H of ''ousing' tells you to drop H. Charles Ives was an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American composer, and to score is to write music.

clue.text: Lettuce served on the White Star Line?

definitions.meaning: a crisp round variety of salad leaf

definitions.text: served on the White Star Line?
definitions.meaning: the White Star Line's Titanic met, or was served, the one that sank her

explanation.surface: Salad leaves dished up to passengers of a famous shipping company.
explanation.walkthrough: The White Star Line owned the Titanic, sunk by an iceberg in 1912: it was 'served' one in a darker sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceberg is a crisp variety of lettuce, and also the floating ice that sank the Titanic.

clue.text: Joshua led rebellious, suspicious peers through this?

indicators.note: rebellious letters refuse to stay in order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Joshua led an uprising, and the wary keep watch through a spyhole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' is a verb, not nobles: the suspicious person peers through it. Judas, the betrayer, fits the rebellious surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A Judas-hole is a small peephole in a door through which a wary person can look out.

clue.text: Busting a gut? Sue the clown!

indicators.note: busting breaks the letters apart, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone laughing fit to burst threatens to take a clown to court.
explanation.definitionFit: An auguste is a type of circus clown, the clumsy one with garish make-up.

clue.text: Dying face up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' sends the letters upwards, so they are read backwards

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock
low means down, as in low spirits

explanation.surface: A body lies face up, then face down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face up' reads as lying on one's back, but splits into the clock-face word and the instruction to read it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone laid low has been struck down, close to death or dying.

clue.text: Lucentio's Mrs MacNab losing head over trapping one

indicators.note: the turned letters trap another letter inside them
in a down clue 'over' means the letters are written upwards, reading backwards
the printed word loses its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean husband's wife is a Mrs MacNab who has lost her head.
explanation.walkthrough: MACNAB loses its head M ('losing head') to give ACNAB, turned by 'over' to BANCA, trapping I. Lucentio marries Bianca in The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Taming of the Shrew, Lucentio woos and marries Bianca, Katherina's younger sister.

clue.text: Rock group supporter, Bunthorne? Get a life! Is this how things start?

parts.note: the setter's pseudonym, so the setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: the start of each of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: The setter is told to get a life by someone mocking rock groups and their fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock group' suggests a band, but means a group of standing stones such as Stonehenge, held up by great stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalith is a large standing stone, one of those that make up and support prehistoric monuments.

clue.text: Good liar could be caught by a stinker!

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged, signalling an anagram

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A good liar may yet be caught out by a rotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinker' looks like a rotter catching the liar, but means something smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic is notoriously pungent, so it is a stinker in the literal sense of smelling strongly.

clue.text: In which one's straightened out from severe habits

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone recovers from bad habits in a treatment centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is a rehabilitation centre, where addicts are helped to straighten out.

clue.text: Sorely pressed with such a headache?

definitions.text: Sorely pressed with such a headache?

parts.words: Sorely pressed with such a headache?
parts.note: a fakir's board studded with spikes presses painfully on the one lying there; nail heads ache

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure suffers a pounding headache.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a board of spikes presses sorely on the body, and each spike has a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed of nails is a fakir's spiked board, and figuratively a painfully difficult situation.

clue.text: See 1 across
Tripping silver tongue works overtime to trip blatherskite

indicators.note: tripping tumbles the letters over, so they are read backwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: the second piece also trips over, read backwards

parts.note: someone whose tongue works overtime gabs, chatters endlessly

explanation.surface: A silver-tongued talker trips over their own words while trying to trip up another chatterbox.
explanation.walkthrough: AG tripped by 'Tripping' gives GA; GABS tripped by 'to trip' gives SBAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A blatherskite is a person who talks foolishly at length, a windbag.

clue.text: Admiral signed up at the Hawkins' tavern

definitions.meaning: John ... was an English admiral of the late 1600s

definitions.text: signed up at the Hawkins' tavern
definitions.meaning: the inn run by Jim Hawkins's family in Treasure Island bore the Admiral's name on its sign

explanation.surface: A naval officer enlists at a pub run by the Hawkins family.
explanation.walkthrough: In Stevenson's Treasure Island, Jim Hawkins's parents keep the Admiral Benbow inn, whose name is on its sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Benbow names both the historical English admiral and the inn sign in Treasure Island.
